0.0.n: A standard daytime greeting; its final は is pronounced わ.

0.2.n: This is the speaker’s name, written in Latin letters.

0.3.n: A polite sentence ending used here to introduce oneself; the speaker leaves out 私は.

1.0.n: A neutral, polite way to refer to yourself.

1.1.n: Marks 私 as the topic: the person this sentence is about.

1.2.n: 匹 counts small animals; 6匹 is read ろっぴき and counts the hamsters here.

1.3.n: Links the animal count to ハムスター, the animals being counted.

1.4.n: Japanese nouns do not change for plural; 6匹 tells you there are six.

1.5.n: Joins the hamsters and cats into one list.

1.6.n: 匹 counts small animals; 6匹 is read ろっぴき and counts the cats here.

1.7.n: Links the animal count to 猫, the animals being counted.

1.8.n: The noun itself does not mark plural; the number supplies that information.

1.9.n: Marks the entire hamster-and-cat group as the companions the speaker lives with.

1.10.n: 暮らす becomes 暮らして + います, politely describing an ongoing living situation.

2.0.n: Sets the starting point for what the speaker will do next.

2.1.n: Names the language; 語 means language.

2.2.n: Marks Japanese as the language used for telling the stories.

3.0.n: Combines with たち to include the speaker and others, here the pets.

3.1.n: Added to 私 to make 私たち, meaning we.

3.2.n: Links 私たち to the happy days, showing whose days they are.

3.3.n: Describes 日々 and needs な when placed directly before this noun.

3.4.n: Connects 幸せ to the noun 日々; it has no separate English equivalent.

3.5.n: 々 repeats the preceding character; 日々 refers to day-to-day life here.

3.6.n: Marks the happy days as the subject matter of the speaker’s storytelling.

3.7.n: お adds politeness to 話し; していきます politely presents telling as something continuing into the future.

0.tip: Japanese commonly leaves out I when the speaker’s identity is clear.

1.lit: As for me, six hamsters and six cats with, am living.
1.tip: The first と joins the animals with and; the second と marks them as companions with with.

2.tip: で marks the language used, and this unfinished phrase continues into the next line.

3.lit: Our happy days, will go on telling about.
3.tip: A verb’s て-form plus いきます can describe an action continuing forward in time, rather than physical movement.
